title: Baptism of Mieszko I
description: Duke Mieszko I accepts Latin Christianity, the event traditionally taken as the beginning of the Polish state.

title: Congress of Gniezno
description: Emperor Otto III meets Bolesław the Brave at the tomb of Saint Adalbert and an archbishopric is set up at Gniezno, giving Poland its own church province.

title: Bolesław the Brave crowned king
description: Bolesław I is crowned the first king of Poland a few weeks before his death.

title: Testament of Bolesław III
description: On his death Bolesław III divides the realm among his sons, beginning almost two centuries of rule by rival Piast dukes.

title: Battle of Legnica
description: A Mongol army defeats and kills Duke Henry II the Pious of Silesia, ending the best chance of an early reunification of the Polish duchies.

title: Władysław the Elbow-high crowned
description: Władysław I is crowned at Wawel Cathedral, restoring a united Polish kingdom after the period of division.

title: University of Kraków founded
description: Casimir III the Great founds the university later called the Jagiellonian, the oldest in Poland.

title: Union of Krewo
description: Grand Duke Jogaila of Lithuania agrees to accept baptism and marry Queen Jadwiga, joining Poland and Lithuania under one ruler.

title: Battle of Grunwald
description: The Polish and Lithuanian armies defeat the Teutonic Order in one of the largest battles of medieval Europe, breaking the Order's power.

title: Second Peace of Thorn
description: The Thirteen Years' War ends with the Teutonic Order ceding Gdańsk and western Prussia to Poland, which regains access to the Baltic.

title: Prussian Homage
description: Albert of Hohenzollern, the last grand master of the Teutonic Order in Prussia, swears fealty to Sigismund I as a secular Lutheran duke.

title: Copernicus publishes On the Revolutions
description: Nicolaus Copernicus, a canon at Frombork, publishes the book that places the Sun at the centre of the planets, and dies the same year.

title: Union of Lublin
description: Poland and Lithuania are joined in a single Commonwealth with one elected king and one parliament.

title: Warsaw Confederation
description: The nobility guarantees religious toleration in the Commonwealth, an unusual grant in the Europe of the wars of religion.

title: Siege of Jasna Góra
description: The monastery of Jasna Góra holds out against a Swedish army during the invasion known as the Deluge, which devastated the Commonwealth.

title: First Partition of Poland
description: Russia, Prussia and Austria sign the treaty by which each takes a share of the Commonwealth's territory.

title: Constitution of 3 May
description: The Great Sejm adopts a written constitution, generally counted the first in modern Europe, in an attempt to reform the Commonwealth.

title: Battle of Racławice
description: Tadeusz Kościuszko's insurgents, including peasants armed with scythes, defeat a Russian force early in the uprising against the partitioning powers.

title: Third Partition of Poland
description: Russia, Prussia and Austria divide what is left of the Commonwealth, and Poland disappears from the map for 123 years.

title: Duchy of Warsaw created
description: By the Treaties of Tilsit Napoleon forms a Polish state from lands Prussia had taken in the partitions.

title: November Uprising
description: Cadets attack the Belweder Palace and begin a rising against Russian rule that is put down the next year.

title: January Uprising
description: A rising against Russian rule begins and is fought as a guerrilla war until 1864, followed by harsh Russification.

title: Independence regained
description: Józef Piłsudski takes command of Polish forces in Warsaw as the German occupation collapses, the day kept as Poland's independence day.

title: Battle of Warsaw
description: The Polish army throws back the Red Army at the gates of Warsaw, deciding the Polish–Soviet War.

title: May Coup
description: Piłsudski overthrows the elected government after three days of fighting and rules in effect until his death in 1935.

title: Katyn massacre
description: The Soviet NKVD shoots about 22,000 captured Polish officers and officials at Katyn and other sites.

title: Warsaw Uprising
description: The Home Army rises against the German occupation and fights for 63 days, after which the city is systematically destroyed.

title: Poznań protests
description: Workers' demonstrations are put down by the army with dozens of deaths, leading to a change of party leadership in October.

title: John Paul II elected pope
description: Karol Wojtyła, archbishop of Kraków, becomes the first Polish pope, and his visit home the next year draws millions.

title: Gdańsk Agreement
description: After a strike at the Lenin Shipyard led by Lech Wałęsa the government accepts independent trade unions, from which Solidarity is formed.

title: Martial law declared
description: General Jaruzelski imposes martial law, bans Solidarity and interns thousands of its members.

title: Partly free elections
description: Solidarity wins almost every seat it is allowed to contest, leading to the first non-communist government in the Soviet bloc.

title: Poland joins the European Union
description: Poland enters the European Union with nine other states, five years after joining NATO.

title: Smolensk air disaster
description: President Lech Kaczyński and 95 others die when their aircraft crashes on the way to a Katyn commemoration.
